title: FTUE / first-run activation program (pre-launch)
description:
FTUE / first-run activation program (pre-launch). Full analysis: research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md.

AHA MOMENT: a new user's first recorded RANKED match result that moves their ELO off the bare starting 1000 (the first time a meaningful, earned rating becomes real). NOT 'finished profile', NOT 'saw ELO 1000'.

ACTIVATION MILESTONE (instrumentable): athlete_activated = backend trigger flips pending->active on an athletes UPDATE supplying display_name + current_weight + (primary_gym_id OR free_agent) + gender + date_of_birth (detect at use-setup-submit.ts:112-121).

CURRENT TTV (mobile): ~6 taps / realistically ~10-12 with in-wizard controls, 10 fields, plus an out-of-app email round trip if confirmation is ON. The aha endpoint is currently UNREACHABLE by a solo user (challenge stubbed, sessions gym-manager-gated).

PROGRAM = 3 parallel tracks: (a) make the endpoint reachable (seed a launch gym), (b) make it measurable (instrument the funnel), (c) remove client friction + de-motivators (quick wins). Sequence: Week 0 seed+instrument; Week 1 client-only quick wins (no new build); Week 1-2 config/web; next EAS build for native-gated items. Apple Sign In = jits-rag (4.8 compliance, must precede public Google-on-signup).
design: Respect dark-first Void theme, Signal-Red for CTAs/negative only, numeric data never red, sharp 4px corners, minimal motion, 4 purpose-bound fonts. Do NOT change activation-trigger logic or write guarded athlete columns.
acceptance_criteria: Quick-win client release shipped (no new EAS build); funnel instrumented end-to-end; launch gym seeded with a joinable session; activation rate measurable as a windowed rate.

title: TestFlight launch crash: native TurboModule throws NSException at launch, corrupting Hermes (newArch)

1. expo-secure-store getItemAsync via Supabase auth getSession -- lib/supabase/secure-storage.ts:27 <- lib/auth/auth-context.tsx:57. Keychain entitlement / keychain-access-group mismatch from unfinished eas init / provisioning. NOT try/catch-wrapped at the JS boundary.

Both consistent with the open pre-launch blocker: eas init placeholders + unfinished Apple provisioning (Team ID, push key, entitlements).

Sentry not in the crash stack (initSentry early-returns without DSN; lib/error-tracking/sentry.ts). (a) Release build on-device: npx expo run:ios --configuration Release, read '*** Terminating app due to uncaught exception' in Xcode/Console; OR
(b) Console.app / idevicesyslog filtered to process ELORATED during TestFlight launch; OR

Then: fix the named module's entitlement/config AND wrap launch-path native calls (SecureStore getItem, notification handler setup) in try/catch so a native throw degrades instead of crashing.

title: Mobile confirm step can strand a user on 'waiting for opponent to confirm' if the opponent's result_confirmed broadcast is missed
description:
FOUND during live simulator walkthrough. In the session flow record_match_result completes the match (+applies ELO) BEFORE the confirm step mounts. use-match-completion.ts advances only on (a) a fresh postgres_changes UPDATE to completed/disputed (already happened at record time -> missed), or (b) a matchStatus PROP that is stale 'pending'/'in_progress' from the wizard's initial fetch (match-flow-wizard fetches once, doesn't refetch until confirm onCompleted). So the user relies solely on the opponent's realtime result_confirmed broadcast (confirm-step.tsx onResultConfirmed). If that broadcast is missed (opponent confirmed before this client subscribed, reconnect, or - here - the NPC exited), the user is stuck on 'WAITING FOR OPPONENT TO CONFIRM...' forever even though the match is fully completed in the DB.

Works in the common case (two live humans both present exchange broadcasts). NOTE: naive fix (advance whenever match is completed on mount) is WRONG - it would auto-skip the confirm/dispute window for everyone since the match is always completed by record time. Recommended: on confirm-step mount, reconcile opponent confirmation from match_confirmations (RLS permitting) and/or once THIS athlete has confirmed, advance independently of the opponent (the match is already finalized; opponent acks on their own device; summary already handles a later disputed status). Needs design decision on confirm semantics before implementing.

title: Gym list 'LIVE' vs detail 'No Sessions' inconsistency (dead-end)
description:
Gym LIST and gym DETAIL use DIFFERENT filters for what counts as a live/joinable session, so a gym can show 'LIVE' on the list but 'No Sessions Scheduled' in detail — a dead end.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed), both in packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:
- getGymsWithSessions (line 452): flags hasActiveSession purely on sessions.status='active' (lines 472, 490-491, 512). It does NOT check scheduled_end. Drives gym-card.tsx LivePill (gym.hasActiveSession, gym-card.tsx:28).
- getGymDetail (line 526): fetches sessions with status IN ('scheduled','active') AND .gt('scheduled_end', now) (lines 546-548). So an 'active' session whose scheduled_end is already in the past is EXCLUDED from detail, yielding sessionListItems=[] -> mobile renders 'No Sessions Scheduled' (gym-detail-parts.tsx:120). Web (gym-detail-content.tsx) consumes the same query so it has the same dead-end.

PROPOSED FIX: adopt ONE rule in both queries: a session is live/joinable iff status='active' AND scheduled_end > now(). In getGymsWithSessions, when building activeMap (lines 489-491) also require s.scheduled_end > now (add scheduled_end to the select at line 471). This makes hasActiveSession agree with detail. (Alternative considered: relax detail to include past-end active sessions — rejected; a session past its end shouldn't be presented as joinable. Keeping the stricter rule and applying it to the list is the consistent, correct choice.)

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- A gym shows 'LIVE' on the list IFF its detail shows at least one joinable (status=active, scheduled_end>now) session. No gym can be LIVE on the list and empty in detail.
- An 'active' session with scheduled_end in the past is treated as not-live by BOTH queries.
- Existing unit tests for these queries updated/added to cover the past-scheduled_end case.

RISK: low (pure query-filter change in shared, no schema change).
SCOPE: shared (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts) — both web and mobile inherit the fix automatically (web parity is automatic).

title: Add a merged 'How rating works' explainer in plain BJJ language (anchored to ELO inline copy)
description:
PROBLEM: The core value (a meaningful rating) is expressed in chess/programmer jargon: 'ELO 1000', 'ranked vs casual', 'Pressure Score', 'weight_division_gap +50 phantom ELO', with no BJJ-native anchor. The competitor persona understands belt/stripe/weight class/open mat instantly but not these terms. If the rating does not map to what they feel in the gym, the number is noise and they will not trust or chase it, and trust in the rating IS the product.

EVIDENCE: CLAUDE.md business rules (weight-aware +50/division, draws cost both via Pressure Score, casual does not change rating); competitor persona jargon list; research: goal-matched, value-mapped explanation reduces the 'this number is noise' bounce (https://www.airbridge.io/en/blog/social-proof-for-apps)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Client-only content. MERGE with the inline ELO anchor (the 0%/ELO-anchor quick win): keep the one-line anchor inline on the EloTile, and put the fuller explanation behind a single dismissible info affordance off the tile, ONE static screen, not a multi-screen tutorial. Copy in gym language: 'Everyone starts at 1000. Win ranked matches to climb. Beat someone heavier or higher-rated and you gain more. Casual rolls don't change your rating; ranked matches do. Draws cost both athletes a little.' CONTENT-CORRECTNESS RISK: pull the exact rules from the BE FRONTEND_INTEGRATION_GUIDE / research/005, do not paraphrase from memory, wrong rules destroy trust. Brand: amber for draws, green only for gains, no red on numbers. Do NOT auto-assign a belt from ELO.

Group: Medium | Effort S | Impact Low. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #14).

title: Unify the three progress counters into one continuous, entry-path-aware label
description:
PROBLEM: The user crosses three disconnected counters: login shows none, signup says 'Step 1 of 2 / Account', then the wizard restarts at 'Step 1 of 3'. The real journey is ~4 steps; each counter implies near-completion then resets, undermining the goal-gradient pull progress meters are meant to create.

EVIDENCE: signup.tsx:96 ('Step 1 of 2 / Account'); wizard-progress.tsx:21 ('Step 1 of 3'); login has no counter; research: progress bars lift multi-step conversion (https://foundrycro.com/blog/form-conversion-rate-benchmarks-2026/)

PROPOSED CHANGE: Adopt one continuous static counter across signup->activation: signup '1 of 4', TOS '2 of 4', Identity '3 of 4', Training '4 of 4, almost there'. Keep it a static mono label / segmented bar (no animated fill) per the motion rule. CRITICAL per critique: the SSO path skips the password-entry portion of signup, so make the counter conditional on entry path (an SSO user effectively starts at the wizard), or it will lie to SSO users. The two surfaces are separate route groups ((auth)/signup vs profile-setup), so the offset must be passed/recomputed across the navigation boundary.

AFFECTED: apps/mobile/app/(auth)/signup.tsx, apps/mobile/components/profile-setup/wizard-progress.tsx, apps/mobile/components/profile-setup/setup-wizard.tsx

Group: QuickWin | Effort S | Impact Low. From research/012-ftue-discovery-roadmap.md (rec #8).
acceptance_criteria: A continuous 'Step N of 4' label appears across signup and the wizard with no reset to 'Step 1' mid-journey ; The counter is correct for the email path (starts at 1) and the SSO path (does not claim a skipped step) ; The indicator is static (no animation) per the minimal-motion rule

title: Improve Gyms tab load performance + loading UX
description:
The Gyms tab feels slow/unresponsive on first open (observed live on iOS sim). Root causes found in code review:

1. getGymsWithSessions() (packages/shared/src/api/queries.ts:452) runs THREE sequential, independent network round-trips (gyms -> athletes -> sessions). They have no data dependency and should be Promise.all'd. Biggest win: ~3x -> ~1x latency.
2. The Gyms screen hook useGymsList() (apps/mobile/app/(app)/(tabs)/gyms/index.tsx:48) fires a 4th query for gym coords (id, latitude, longitude) that duplicates the gyms table read already done in getGymsWithSessions step 1. Fold latitude/longitude into that first select to drop a round-trip.
3. No caching / no stale-while-revalidate. Every first mount pays full latency and shows a bare centered ActivityIndicator. Consider a lightweight shared cache so re-navigation is instant, and show cached data immediately while refreshing in background.

Loading UX improvements to make broadly (not just Gyms):
- Replace bare centered spinners with skeleton placeholders (perceived performance).
- Stale-while-revalidate pattern for list screens so navigating back to a tab is instant.
- Audit other tabs (Rankings/leaderboard, Home, Profile) for the same sequential-query and no-cache patterns.
notes: Surfaced during live iOS-sim debug session 2026-05-29. Measure before/after with timing instrumentation. Web app may share getGymsWithSessions so verify both consumers.

title: Runtime warning: Supabase auth token > 2048 bytes in SecureStore (chunked adapter)
description:
Persistent yellow warning: 'Value being stored in SecureStore is larger than 2048 bytes ...'. The Supabase auth session payload (access+refresh token + user metadata) exceeds expo-secure-store's 2048-byte soft warning limit.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed): apps/mobile/lib/supabase/secure-storage.ts SecureStoreAdapter.setItem (line 29-35) writes the whole serialized session to a single SecureStore key via SecureStore.setItemAsync; expo-secure-store warns above ~2048 bytes. The adapter's own doc-comment (lines 14-21) anticipates this and names the LargeSecureStore pattern as the fix.

PROPOSED FIX: implement a CHUNKED SecureStore adapter — split the value into <2048-byte chunks across keys (e.g. ${key}.0, ${key}.1, ... plus a ${key}.meta count), reassemble on getItem, and delete all chunks on removeItem. Keep the web localStorage branch unchanged. CRITICAL: do NOT regress the cold-start auth-lock fix (CHANGELOG/git 322039e + beads memory 'mobile-supabase-auth-lock-coldstart'): the adapter must remain a drop-in async storage; processLock and the synchronous onAuthStateChange callback in auth-context.tsx must be untouched; getItem must reliably return the full reassembled value (a partial/empty read at cold start could wedge the Loading gate). Add migration handling: if an old single-key value exists, read it, re-chunk on next write (or read-through then delete). Alternative (encrypt-to-AsyncStorage LargeSecureStore) is heavier and adds AsyncStorage dependency — prefer pure chunked SecureStore.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- No 'larger than 2048 bytes' warning after sign-in/refresh on mobile.
- Session persists across cold start (sign in, force-quit, reopen -> still authenticated, no Loading hang).
- Token rotation (autoRefreshToken) updates all chunks; sign-out clears all chunks (no orphans).
- No regression to the cold-start auth lock fix; processLock + sync onAuthStateChange unchanged.
- Existing/added unit test for the adapter round-trips a >2KB value across chunks.

RISK: med (auth persistence + cold-start path is the previously-fragile area). Requires a new EAS build to verify on device (native-adjacent).
SCOPE: mobile only (apps/mobile/lib/supabase/secure-storage.ts). No web parity (web uses localStorage).
close_reason: Implemented + independently reviewed + quality gate green (typecheck, jits_web tests 389, web build, jr_be 038 test all pass).

title: Runtime warning: Realtime send() falling back to REST (use httpSend or join before send)
description:
Persistent yellow warning toast: 'Realtime send() is automatically falling back to REST API. ... Please use httpSend() explicitly for REST delivery.'

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in @supabase/realtime-js 2.105.4, RealtimeChannel.js:487-492): channel.send({type:'broadcast',...}) warns + REST-falls-back whenever the channel can't push over the websocket (!canPush()) — i.e. the broadcast fires before the channel has finished JOIN, or on a channel not configured for WS broadcast. Our broadcast senders that hit this:
- packages/shared/src/hooks/use-session-match-sync.ts:60 (channelRef.current?.send({type:'broadcast',event,payload})) — used by the ready step (broadcastReady) and timer/result events; readiness broadcasts commonly fire right at mount before join completes.
- packages/shared/src/hooks/use-match-sync.ts:55,63,71
- packages/shared/src/hooks/use-lobby-sync.ts:80,88,96
- apps/mobile/components/session/wizard/confirm-step.tsx:86 (await channel.send(...))

PROPOSED FIX (supabase-js-correct): for these fire-and-forget broadcasts, call channel.httpSend(event, payload) explicitly (the API the warning recommends; present in 2.105.4, RealtimeChannel.d.ts:355) instead of send({type:'broadcast'}). This is the intended REST path and silences the warning. Alternatively/additionally, gate sends on the channel being SUBSCRIBED (track subscribe status and queue/drop until 'SUBSCRIBED') so WS push is used when available. Prefer httpSend for the one-shot lobby/ready/result events; keep send for events guaranteed to fire post-join. Apply consistently across the shared hooks so web and mobile both stop warning.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- No 'send() falling back to REST' warning during lobby join, ready-check, and result broadcast on mobile.
- Broadcast events still deliver (opponent still sees ready/challenge/match/result events).
- Change lives in shared hooks; web behavior unchanged functionally and also warning-free.

RISK: low/med (realtime delivery semantics; verify opponent still receives events).
SCOPE: shared (use-session-match-sync.ts, use-match-sync.ts, use-lobby-sync.ts) + apps/mobile/components/session/wizard/confirm-step.tsx. WEB PARITY automatic (shared hooks consumed by both).
close_reason: Implemented + independently reviewed + quality gate green (typecheck, jits_web tests 389, web build, jr_be 038 test all pass).

title: EUA/edit-profile re-prompt inconsistency for active athletes (seed-data artifact)
description:
Reported: an athlete with status='active' but missing gender/dob/city and no waiver_acknowledgements row was routed into the 3-step EDIT PROFILE wizard on explicit login, but on cold relaunch went straight to home.

INVESTIGATION (confirmed in code): On MOBILE there is NO such inconsistency. Both explicit login (apps/mobile/app/(auth)/login.tsx onSubmit/onGooglePress call router.replace('/')) and cold relaunch funnel through the SAME guard, apps/mobile/app/index.tsx, which routes to /profile-setup ONLY when !athlete || status===PENDING (index.tsx:18-21); an 'active' athlete always goes to /(app)/(home) in BOTH paths. No mobile login path routes an active-but-incomplete athlete into the EDIT PROFILE wizard. The EDIT PROFILE wizard (isEditing, use-setup-data.ts:117) is reachable only by explicitly navigating to /profile-setup (e.g. from settings). The reported login-into-wizard behavior is a WEB behavior (the /eua route exists only on web: apps/web/app/(auth)/eua/).

REACHABILITY: A real MOBILE user reaches status='active' only by completing the wizard (TOS/EUA -> identity gender+dob -> training weight+gym+city), so a real active user already has gender/dob/city + a waiver_acknowledgement. An active row missing those fields is a SEED-DATA artifact (jr_be seed sets status directly, bypassing handle_athlete_activation + the wizard).

RECOMMENDATION (lowest-risk): For the mobile scope of this sprint, CLOSE-AS-WONT-FIX / not-a-bug (no mobile code defect). If the web /eua + login routing shows the actual divergence, file a WEB-scoped issue to make web's login routing consistent with its cold-start guard. Separately, recommend fixing the jr_be seed so seeded 'active' athletes carry gender/date_of_birth/city + a waiver_acknowledgements row (so verification doesn't hit phantom states). Do not change mobile index.tsx — adding a fields-complete check there would force real-but-edge users (and every seed account) into the wizard and risks an activation loop given the athlete-column guard trigger.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Documented decision: mobile = no code change (not a bug). 
- (If pursued) jr_be seed produces complete active athletes, OR a separate web issue tracks web login/guard consistency.

RISK: low (decision/doc; optional seed fix in jr_be).
SCOPE: investigation/decision. Optional: jr_be seed; optional separate web issue. Mobile: no change.
close_reason: Not a mobile bug: seed-data artifact. Mobile login and cold-start both use the status-only guard in apps/mobile/app/index.tsx, so an 'active' athlete always routes home on both paths; the EUA re-prompt is web-only and a real mobile user reaches 'active' only by completing the wizard. Optional follow-ups (separate issues if desired): (a) jr_be seed completeness (gender/dob/city + waiver_acknowledgements), (b) web login/guard parity.
